On Tuesday, September 11, 2012 12:14:21 PM UTC+2, Andrej wrote:
Dear knitRs,

I came accross an issuee with compiling LaTeX "exam" document producing with knitr. Pasted below is minimal reproducible code.

Knitr compiles fine, but pdflatex terminated with:
 - Command \framed already defined.
 - Command \shaded already defined.
 - Command \leftbox already defined.

Thanks in advance for any pointers or ideas.

Best, Andrej

%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%
\documentclass[a4paper,11pt,addpoints]{exam}
\usepackage[utf8]{inputenc}
\usepackage[T1]{fontenc}
\begin{document}
\begin{questions}

\question[1]
Test question.

<<test-chunk>>=
bla <- 1+1
@

\begin{choices}
\choice ans1
\choice ans2
\choice ans3
\end{choices}

\begin{solution}
a
\end{solution}

\end{questions}
\end{document}
%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%

messages.subject: Re: [knitr] Re: Exam class issue with knitr
parts:
Although you have got the answer on TEX.SE
(http://tex.stackexchange.com/q/71177/9128), here is a knitr solution,
which removes \usepackage{framed} from the preamble:

\documentclass{exam}

\begin{document}
<<include=FALSE>>=
knit_hooks$set(document=function(x){
sub('\\usepackage{framed}', '', x, fixed=TRUE)
})
@

<<>>=
1+1
@

asdf

\end{document}

Regards,
Yihui

messages.subject: Re: [knitr] Re: Exam class issue with knitr
parts:
Good question! In that case, the `document` hook needs to do one more
thing like:

if (file.exists('knitr.sty')) {
sty = readLines('knitr.sty')
sty = sub('\\usepackage{framed}', '', sty, fixed=TRUE)
writeLines(sty, 'knitr.sty')

}
